## Purpose and model

This read-only notebook introduces the reusable viewer-activity tools. The
canonical stored grain is one row per **talent, video, and identified chatter**
in `analysis.viewer_video_activity`; it is refreshed by
`r_scripts/run/publish_viewer_activity.R`.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  U[User / chatter] -->|message_count| V[Video]
  V -->|hosted by| S[Streamer / talent]
```

The blue user--video edge represents collected chat participation, and its
weight is messages sent in that video. The streamer link is ownership context,
not engagement. This network does not represent viewers who watched without
chatting.

| Field | Supports | Does not prove |
|---|---|---|
| First observed chat | Earliest collected stream chat | First watch or original community entry |
| Public subscription date | Date reported in a matched public subscriber snapshot | Complete subscriber coverage or paid membership start |
| Membership event | Observed `membership_item` chat event | Original or uninterrupted membership |

## Reusable tools

The notebook is deliberately thin. Reusable responsibilities live in the
library so reports, dashboards, and the Analyze Talent Data workflow can use
the same definitions.

| Tool area | Main functions | Responsibility |
|---|---|---|
| `lib/import_data/viewer_activity.R` | `load_viewer_video_activity()`, `load_viewer_profiles()` | Canonical lakehouse reads |
| `lib/dashboard/metrics/viewer_activity.R` | `viewer_activity_talent_summary()`, `viewer_activity_video_summary()` | General engagement numbers and participant tables |
| `lib/plots/domains/audience/viewer_activity.R` | `viewer_activity_bipartite_prep()`, `viewer_activity_bipartite_ggplot()` | Network-ready tables and graph rendering |

The stored `analysis.viewer_profiles` and `analysis.global_viewer_profiles`
tables remain the reusable per-talent and cross-talent descriptive layers.
User--user co-participation is a later, derived projection of the canonical
user--video edges; it is not stored as a second edge table.

## Parameters

- `talent_code`: one exact talent code; null includes all talents.
- `video_id`: focus the participant table and network on one video.
- `bipartite_max_videos` / `bipartite_max_users`: display bounds for a readable graph.
- `network_label_count`: maximum user labels; all displayed videos and streamers are labeled.

## Setup and audit

```{r}
required_packages <- c("DBI", "duckdb", "dplyr", "ggplot2", "here", "knitr", "scales")
missing_packages <- required_packages[!vapply(required_packages, requireNamespace, logical(1), quietly = TRUE)]
if (length(missing_packages) > 0L) {
  stop("Install the required R packages before rendering: ", paste(missing_packages, collapse = ", "), call. = FALSE)
}

suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(dplyr))
source(here::here("r_scripts", "lib", "utils", "repo_env.R"))
source(here::here("r_scripts", "lib", "utils", "datalake_root.r"))
source(here::here("r_scripts", "lib", "duckdb", "db_connect.R"))
source(here::here("r_scripts", "lib", "import_data", "viewer_activity.R"))
source(here::here("r_scripts", "lib", "dashboard", "metrics", "viewer_activity.R"))
source(here::here("r_scripts", "lib", "plots", "domains", "audience", "viewer_activity.R"))

load_repo_env(repo_root = here::here())
db_path <- talent_lakehouse_db_path()
if (!file.exists(db_path)) stop("Unified talent lakehouse not found: ", db_path, call. = FALSE)
con <- duckdb_connect(db_path = db_path, read_only = TRUE)

normalize_parameter <- function(value) {
  if (is.null(value) || length(value) == 0L || is.na(value[[1]])) return(NULL)
  value <- trimws(as.character(value[[1]]))
  if (nzchar(value)) value else NULL
}
display_table <- function(rows, digits = 1L) {
  if (nrow(rows) == 0L) return(knitr::kable(data.frame(message = "No rows matched.")))
  knitr::kable(rows, digits = digits)
}
positive_parameter <- function(value, default) {
  value <- suppressWarnings(as.integer(value))
  if (is.na(value) || value < 1L) default else value
}
talent_code <- normalize_parameter(params$talent_code)
video_id <- normalize_parameter(params$video_id)
profile_preview_limit <- positive_parameter(params$profile_preview_limit, 50L)
bipartite_max_videos <- positive_parameter(params$bipartite_max_videos, 12L)
bipartite_max_users <- positive_parameter(params$bipartite_max_users, 60L)
network_label_count <- positive_parameter(params$network_label_count, 15L)

required_relations <- data.frame(schema_name = c("text", "catalog", "clean", "analysis", "analysis", "analysis"), relation_name = c("chat_messages", "videos", "public_subscriber_snapshots", "viewer_video_activity", "viewer_profiles", "global_viewer_profiles"))
available_relations <- DBI::dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT table_schema AS schema_name, table_name AS relation_name FROM information_schema.tables")
required_relations <- required_relations %>% left_join(available_relations %>% mutate(available = TRUE), by = c("schema_name", "relation_name")) %>% mutate(available = coalesce(.data$available, FALSE), status = if_else(.data$available, "PASS", "FAIL"))
display_table(required_relations)
if (!all(required_relations$available)) stop("Run the viewer activity publisher before rendering.", call. = FALSE)
```

## Load the canonical activity and profile layers

```{r}
viewer_video_activity <- load_viewer_video_activity(con, talent_code) %>%
  mutate(stream_at = as.POSIXct(.data$stream_at, tz = "UTC"), active_minutes = .data$active_span_seconds / 60)
viewer_profiles <- load_viewer_profiles(con, talent_code) %>%
  mutate(observed_span_days = as.numeric(difftime(.data$last_observed_stream_at, .data$first_observed_stream_at, units = "days")))
if (nrow(viewer_video_activity) == 0L) stop("No collected chat activity matched the selected scope.", call. = FALSE)

display_table(data.frame(item = c("Database", "Talent scope", "User–video edges"), value = c(db_path, if (is.null(talent_code)) "All talents" else talent_code, nrow(viewer_video_activity))))
```

## Reusable engagement numbers

These numbers come from `viewer_activity_talent_summary()`, so downstream
workflows can use the same definitions without copying notebook calculations.

```{r}
talent_summary <- viewer_activity_talent_summary(viewer_profiles, viewer_video_activity)
display_table(talent_summary %>% mutate(messages = scales::comma(.data$messages), public_subscription_coverage = scales::percent(.data$public_subscription_coverage, accuracy = 0.1)))

video_summary <- viewer_activity_video_summary(viewer_video_activity)
display_table(slice_head(video_summary, n = 20L))

if (!is.null(video_id)) {
  display_table(viewer_activity_video_participants(viewer_video_activity, video_id, profile_preview_limit))
}
```

## User–video engagement graph

`viewer_activity_bipartite_prep()` returns ordinary node and edge tables as
well as the graph-ready coordinates. Use those tables directly in a dashboard,
table, or another graphing system; this notebook uses the paired ggplot helper.

```{r}
engagement_network <- viewer_activity_bipartite_prep(
  viewer_video_activity,
  video_id = video_id,
  max_videos = bipartite_max_videos,
  max_users = bipartite_max_users
)

display_table(slice_head(engagement_network$engagement_edges %>% select(.data$user_id, .data$video_id, .data$message_count), n = 20L))

engagement_plot <- viewer_activity_bipartite_ggplot(engagement_network, network_label_count)
if (is.null(engagement_plot)) {
  plot.new()
  graphics::text(0.5, 0.5, "No user–video chat edges matched the selected scope.")
} else {
  print(engagement_plot)
}
```

## Profile review surface

```{r}
profile_preview <- viewer_profiles %>%
  arrange(desc(.data$videos_chatted_in), desc(.data$total_messages), .data$talent_code, .data$user_id) %>%
  select(.data$talent_code, .data$user_id, .data$current_username, .data$first_observed_stream_at, .data$last_observed_stream_at, .data$videos_chatted_in, .data$total_messages, .data$paid_messages, .data$membership_events, .data$subscribed_at, .data$public_subscription_matched, .data$subscription_date_changed) %>%
  slice_head(n = profile_preview_limit)
display_table(profile_preview)
```

## Operating notes

1. Refresh the canonical activity tables with `publish_viewer_activity.R`; it defaults to a dry run.
2. Use the import and metric helpers for repeatable counts in analysis workflows.
3. Use the plotting helper only after selecting a readable scope; do not treat a visual bound as a population filter.
4. Keep subscription dates and first-observed chat dates qualified as described above.

```{r}
#| include: false
DBI::dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)
```
